note: The healthy baseline: recent activity, inside the stage window, plan linked. Every other case is a departure from this one.

The launch-day case. Nothing writes engagement_events yet (migration 0002), so a null history means unobserved, not inactive. Marking this stalled would flag the whole portfolio on day one and train staff to ignore Pulse.
Boundary: exactly AT_RISK_SILENCE_DAYS. Pins the threshold as inclusive so a fencepost change fails here rather than drifting silently.
Boundary: exactly STALLED_SILENCE_DAYS, and inclusive for the same reason. daysInStage sits at the scoping window (21) without exceeding it, so silence alone drives the verdict.
The signal event recency cannot see: an engagement can look busy and still be stuck. Overrunning the stage window stalls it even with activity two days ago.
A raised blocker is worth surfacing on its own — an otherwise perfectly healthy engagement becomes at_risk the moment someone reports being blocked.
Ordering guard. The blocker rule only ever worsens a verdict, so it must not downgrade this from stalled to at_risk — the blocker is appended as a reason while the status holds.
Plenty of healthy engagements predate their assessment, so a missing plan annotates the signal without changing it. Pins that hasPlan is reported, never scored.
U7 may reshape the stage enum. A stage absent from STAGE_WINDOW_DAYS gets no window rather than a default one, so adding a stage by migration cannot silently mark every engagement in it stalled.
Boundary just under AT_RISK_SILENCE_DAYS. Pairs with the 14-day case so the threshold is pinned from both sides; staff should not be nagged a day early.
Boundary just under STALLED_SILENCE_DAYS. Pairs with the 21-day case: one more day of quiet is the difference between a nudge and an escalation.
Stage overrun is strictly greater-than. Sitting exactly at the 21-day scoping window is still on schedule, not stalled.
One day past the scoping window flips the verdict even with activity two days ago. Pins the strict comparison from the overdue side.
Membership has the longest window (90 days). A second stage at its edge guards against a single hard-coded window leaking into the comparison.
Membership at 91 days is overdue. Confirms the per-stage window lookup, not a global default, drives the verdict.
The shortest window (14 days). A new partner stuck at the first meeting is the earliest drop-off staff can act on.
Budget conversations that drag past three weeks usually mean the partner cannot fund the work; staff want that surfaced early.
The ethics committee window is 30 days. Overrun here often means a committee is waiting on the partner or the reverse, and someone needs to chase it.
A partner who is ready for a hackathon but waiting more than 45 days risks losing volunteer momentum.
A blocker with no other history: status stays at_risk (not escalated) and carries both the unobserved-activity and the blocker reason, so staff see why twice over.
Blocker on an already at_risk engagement must not escalate to stalled. The blocker rule only lifts on_track.
Silence alone would be at_risk; the stage overrun stalls it. The silence reason must survive so staff see both causes.
A missing plan never changes the status, but it still annotates an at_risk signal. Guards against the plan check short-circuiting the other reasons.
Missing plan on a stalled engagement keeps it stalled and appends context; plan state is reported, never scored.
Zero-day floor: an engagement created and touched today. Guards against off-by-one on zero silence or zero days in stage.
An unknown stage has no window, but silence rules still apply. The 400 days in stage must not contribute a stage reason.
Unknown stage plus null history: the null-history rule still fires without needing a stage window.
A blocker on a stage overrun: stage rule stalls it first and the blocker is appended, not an escalation of its own.
Silence is just under the at_risk line, so the blocker alone makes the engagement at_risk. Shows the blocker rule works independently of the silence thresholds.
